results.summary_before: This project models a leaky integrate-and-fire neuron using a counter and comparator to generate spikes. It includes a clock divider and a 7-segment display driver to show the counter value, with the lower 8 bits of the counter available on bidirectional pins. The design can be tested by observing the counter increment every second with a 10 MHz clock, and the counting speed can be adjusted via input pins. The documentation is clear but the neuron model is simplified and lacks detailed biological realism.
results.summary: This project uses a 24-bit counter and a programmable compare register to generate a periodic event, with the counter value shown on a 7-segment display. The lower 8 bits of the counter are also available on the bidirectional pins. With all inputs low the compare is set to 10,000,000, so the counter increments once per second at a 10 MHz clock, and setting the inputs programs bits 11 to 18 of the compare value to change the rate. The design can be tested by observing the counter increment every second and experimenting with the input pins to change the counting speed.

results.summary_before: This is a synthesized time-to-digital converter (TDC) that measures the time delay between a start signal and the clock using an interleaved delay line. The captured result is muxed out byte by byte via output pins. It requires two external signal generators to provide the start signal and clock with a known delay. Silicon testing showed partial functionality, with bits changing when a ~7ns delay was applied.
